heroDescription: Trace a franchise that began in Dallas, found its home in Kansas City, and built championship teams in very different eras. These milestones connect the AFL pioneers, Arrowhead's playoff crowds, and the Reid–Mahomes years.

timeline.title: The Dallas Texans take the field
timeline.description: Lamar Hunt's franchise begins play as the Dallas Texans in the American Football League. The team's first season finishes with an 8–6 record.

timeline.title: A championship before the move
timeline.description: Dallas outlasts Houston 20–17 in double overtime on December 23. The franchise's first playoff appearance ends with its first AFL championship.

timeline.title: Kansas City becomes home
timeline.description: Hunt relocates the team and introduces the Chiefs name. Municipal Stadium becomes the setting for the franchise's first Kansas City seasons.

timeline.title: The AFL's first Super Bowl representative
timeline.description: Another AFL title sends Kansas City into the inaugural Super Bowl. The Chiefs lose 35–10 to Green Bay on January 15, 1967.

timeline.title: Super Bowl IV belongs to Kansas City
timeline.description: The Chiefs beat Minnesota 23–7 on January 11, 1970. Hank Stram's team closes its final AFL season with a victory over the NFL champion.

timeline.title: A new stage at Arrowhead
timeline.description: The Chiefs move from Municipal Stadium into Arrowhead. The stadium becomes a defining part of the club's Kansas City identity.

timeline.title: The Schottenheimer chapter begins
timeline.description: Marty Schottenheimer takes over as head coach. His 1989–1998 tenure brings a sustained return to playoff contention.

timeline.title: Montana brings another playoff push
timeline.description: Kansas City trades for Joe Montana. His first Chiefs season includes postseason victories over Pittsburgh and Houston, giving the revival memorable January moments.

timeline.title: Reid opens with a turnaround
timeline.description: Andy Reid's first Kansas City team goes 11–5 and reaches the playoffs, following a 2–14 season. A 9–0 start gives the new coaching era immediate momentum.

timeline.title: Mahomes makes an MVP entrance
timeline.description: In his first season as the full-time starter, Patrick Mahomes throws 50 touchdown passes and wins the franchise's first AP NFL MVP award. Arrowhead hosts its first AFC Championship Game that postseason.

timeline.title: A fifty-year wait ends
timeline.description: Kansas City defeats San Francisco 31–20 in Super Bowl LIV, played in February 2020. The victory delivers the franchise's first league championship in fifty years.

timeline.title: Consecutive seasons, consecutive titles
timeline.description: The Chiefs follow their 2022 championship with another in the 2023 season. Those Super Bowl LVII and LVIII victories make three titles across five seasons for Reid's team.

eras.title: Hunt and Stram's AFL foundation
eras.description: Dallas roots and a Kansas City home frame the franchise's early rise. Hank Stram guides the club through the AFL years, with Len Dawson and a formidable defense helping establish its championship identity.

eras.title: Arrowhead finds its playoff voice
eras.description: Schottenheimer's teams make home-field advantage central to their ambitions. A win over the Raiders in the 1991 postseason gives Arrowhead its first playoff victory and a new set of shared memories.

eras.title: A passing game that changes expectations
eras.description: The 2018 offense joins Mahomes' ambitious passing with production from Travis Kelce and Tyreek Hill. Kansas City scores 565 points and wins a third straight AFC West title.

eras.title: The Reid–Mahomes championship years
eras.description: Super Bowl wins for the 2019, 2022 and 2023 seasons turn sustained contention into a defining era. Steve Spagnuolo's defense supplies an essential part of that success alongside the offense.

The player selection is a cross-era introduction, not a ranking; championship totals are explicitly dated. Follow each source link for the underlying record.
